Selector validation cache: implementation and performance
Recorded 2026-11-01

Native :host-context() argument validation now reuses results during one stylesheet
preparation. The cache borrows native TokenList keys, stores booleans, allocates
only for host-context arguments and is discarded when the rule walk completes.
Both valid and invalid results are cached. Native parsing and compound-selector
checks are unchanged. No CSS strings or parser trees are retained by the cache.

Syntax result unchanged: 16,451 / 18,469 selected assertions pass (89.07%).
Exactly the same 2,018 mismatch keys remain, with zero new failures or exclusions.
No additional assertions were fixed in this performance follow-up.
The 178 dependency blocks and 1,840 unresolved cases remain recorded.

The repeated-argument workload measured preparation 30.35% faster and 7.52-13.78%
fewer allocations. Its aggregate timing change is inconclusive. The variables/
inline workload measured +5.33% initially and +2.96% on repeat; normalization
and retry measured +3.32% and +2.89%. These slowdowns are retained, with host/
code-layout uncertainty, rather than reporting an unconditional performance win.

Validation

305 existing style tests and 32 declaration-validation tests passed. Offline
cargo check passed. The full pinned syntax audit scanned 35,417 files and 32,021
literal helper calls with zero dependency parser panics. Its diagnostic exit 101
is expected while mismatches remain. Test/benchmark sources and all expectation
ledgers are unchanged. Lightning CSS remains unchanged and the sole CSS parser.
No rendering or image-comparison suite was rerun.

Performance

The baseline is the previous 45-assertion selector stage, not the earlier
pre-selector build. Existing benchmark sources were compiled unchanged using
the same frozen native/support artifacts, rustc opt-level=2, debuginfo=0.
Ten workloads, 15 alternating before/after pairs each: 300 primary process runs,
plus 30 repeat runs for the variables/inline slowdown. All are pinned to
CPU 6. CPU frequency/boost and shared-host load are uncontrolled. Positive means
slower. Diagnostic 95% bootstrap intervals use 5,000 resamples of paired median
percentage changes, without multiple-comparison correction. An interval including
zero is inconclusive. EPUB totals sum five fixture medians, not a single page.

Workload                      Paired change    95% bootstrap range    Assessment
cascade-plain                   -1.50%    [  -3.06%,   -0.78%]   speedup
cascade-vars-inline             +5.33%    [  +3.29%,  +72.42%]   slowdown
epub-cold                       -2.01%    [  -7.55%,   +2.56%]   inconclusive
epub-cached                     -2.97%    [ -21.20%,   +0.24%]   inconclusive
selector-cold                   -3.68%    [ -22.16%,   +0.40%]   inconclusive
selector-cached                 -0.37%    [  -6.26%,   +2.26%]   inconclusive
unique-selector-cold            +1.02%    [  -1.59%,  +21.60%]   inconclusive
unique-selector-cached          +4.80%    [  -2.22%,  +41.02%]   inconclusive
normalization                   +3.32%    [  +0.52%,   +5.15%]   slowdown
normalization-retry             +2.89%    [  +1.19%,   +4.09%]   slowdown
cascade-vars-inline-repeat      +2.96%    [  +0.13%,   +7.14%]   slowdown

Repeated selector fixtures use 64 classes with identical :host-context(.scope)
arguments, ::selection, and view-transition :only-child selectors. Unique fixtures
use distinct .scopeN arguments per CSS file. Single-file fixtures expose lookup
cost without reuse. Technical/visual fixtures combine two files with the same
64 arguments, so they still benefit from cross-file reuse.
Both builds accept the same CSS and produce equivalent synthetic matching outcomes.
Cold means uncached author programs with machine/default-CSS caches warmed.

All comparisons, including allocation increases and inconclusive timing changes,
are retained in selector-cache-performance.json. Raw stdout, paired observations
and binary hashes are retained with the compressed raw runs. Shared-host noise
and code layout can affect unrelated stages; these intervals do not isolate
causal cost or establish performance on every document.

Further syntax investigation

The column hover assertion needs specification-version review before a new
rejection is justified. The current Selectors 4 user-action rule also warrants
review of 31 earlier pinned-audit fixes; their original scoped results and statuses
are retained. Sources and exact keys are in selector-followup-review.json.
Other column-chain and native grammar gaps were not changed in this follow-up.

The current production delta is confined to selectors.rs and prepared.rs in the
style crate. No test code, Lightning CSS, renderer/GPUI, expectations, exclusions
or image-comparison changes were introduced. Original registry observations and
earlier reports remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Full baseline source, audit/build logs and binaries: /home/johan/.cache/html-wpt-selector-cache
